newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS might lift fuel surcharges.
newsitem.headline: SAS might lift fuel surcharges.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) said on Friday that it was considering ending fuel surcharges on both passenger and cargo flights, after U.S. airline group Delta dropped the levy on Thursday.
"We are assessing it, but we have not reached any decision," SAS spokesman Knut Lovstuhagen told Reuters.
Lovstuhagen said fuel prices currently were falling, which spoke in favour of a drop of fuel surcharges, but the firm dollar was a drawback.
"The rising dollar has cancelled out the advantage derived from falling fuel prices," Lovstuhagen said.
In November 1996 SAS increased passenger fares by two percent and raised cargo rates by five percent, citing higher fuel costs.
SAS is jointly owned by the governments of Sweden, Denmark and Norway and by private investors.
